transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting really stuck on how my face looks, especially the left side. It looks uneven and kind of puffy to me on video calls, and in photos from salsa, and I know people keep saying they don’t really see what I’m talking about, so maybe I’m making too much of it… but it’s been starting to affect me at work and socially. I just thought I should probably talk to someone before it gets worse.
Have you been doing anything repeatedly to try to make your face look more even or less puffy?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make it a big thing, but I do check it a lot. Before meetings or if I’m going out, I’ll open the camera preview and kind of move around to find a better angle or lighting. I’ll fix my hair over that side of my face, retake pictures more than I should… and sometimes I ask friends, like, “Do I look weird?” or “Does this side look puffy?”  

It sounds a little embarrassing saying it out loud, but it can take a while. Sometimes I end up running late, or I get so drained from trying to make it look okay that I don’t really want to go anymore.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about the appearance of your face when you're not actively looking at it or preparing to go out?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s not a big deal, and I know people say they don’t really notice anything, but my mind still goes back to it. Like I’ll be at work after a video call and keep thinking the left side of my face looked uneven or puffy, or I’ll remember a salsa photo and wonder if everyone else saw it too.

I feel a little silly saying that, because it’s not like I want to be focused on it, but it kind of keeps popping up even when I’m not actively checking. It’s started to get in the way more than I’d like.
Do you feel like you have to do these things, like checking your face or finding a certain angle, or could you stop if you wanted to?

I’d like to think I could stop if I really wanted to… but in the moment it doesn’t feel that simple. Like before a meeting or going out, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to check quickly, and then I’m opening the camera preview again, changing the angle or lighting, fixing my hair around that side, retaking a picture.

I know it probably sounds excessive, sorry. It’s just that I feel like I need it to look acceptable before I can move on. And sometimes I keep asking a friend if I look strange, even when they’ve already answered. I can stop eventually, but sometimes it’s only after I’m already late or so tired from it that I don’t really want to go anymore.
Do you feel like these actions, such as checking your face or finding a certain angle, are something you have to do, or are they something you want to do?

I guess… it feels more like something I have to do, even though I don’t really want to. I mean, I’d rather just get ready and leave like a normal person, but before meetings or going out I keep opening the camera preview, trying different angles or lighting, fixing my hair around that side of my face, retaking pictures.

And then sometimes I ask friends if I look strange, even if I know that’s probably annoying. I’m not doing it because it’s fun or anything. It’s more like I can’t feel okay moving on until I’ve checked enough… and sometimes that means I’m late, or I’m so drained I don’t even want to go anymore. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're in control when you're checking your face or trying to make it look more even?

Not really… I mean, I can make myself stop eventually, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely out of control. But when I’m in it, it feels hard to stop.

Like before a meeting or if I’m going out, I’ll just mean to check once, and then I’m opening the camera preview again and again, changing the angle or the lighting, moving my hair around that side of my face, retaking pictures. And sometimes I’ll ask a friend if I look strange, even though I already kind of know I’ve asked enough.

I feel embarrassed saying that. It just doesn’t feel like a choice in the moment, exactly. I keep going until I’m late or I’m so drained that I don’t even really want to go anymore. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like you're doing these checks out of habit or because you genuinely believe something will go wrong if you don't?

I think it’s… a bit of both, maybe? It’s definitely become kind of a habit before meetings or going out, like I automatically open the camera preview and check the angle or lighting.

But it also feels like if I don’t do it, I’ll go out looking strange and not realize it. So I keep adjusting my hair around that side of my face, retaking pictures, sometimes asking friends if I look weird… even when I know I’m probably overdoing it. I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but it can go on until I’m late or just too drained to want to go. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you would experience significant anxiety if you were prevented from checking your face before a meeting or going out?

Yes… I think I would. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but if I couldn’t check at all before a meeting or going out, I’d feel really unsettled.

Usually I keep opening the camera preview, changing the angle or the lighting, fixing my hair around that side of my face, retaking pictures… and sometimes asking friends if I look strange. If someone stopped me from doing that, I think I’d be pretty anxious and distracted, like I wouldn’t feel ready to leave. Sometimes it already gets to the point where I’m late or too drained to go, which is embarrassing to admit.
Do you feel like you're trying to prevent something bad from happening when you check your face or try to make it look more even?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I think something terrible will happen, exactly, but I’m trying to prevent going into a meeting or out somewhere looking noticeably uneven or strange and not realizing it.

So I’ll check the camera preview, then change the angle or the lighting, fix my hair around that side of my face, take another picture… and then another one. Sometimes I’ll ask a friend if I look weird, even though I feel a bit embarrassed doing that.

It’s like I’m trying to make sure I’m “safe” to be seen, I guess. I know that sounds kind of excessive, but in the moment it feels like if I don’t do it, I might miss something obvious. And then it can go on long enough that I’m late or just worn out and don’t want to go anymore. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like you have a strong urge to perform these checking behaviors?

Yes… I do. I wish I didn’t, because it feels kind of embarrassing to say, but the urge can be really strong.

Before a meeting or going out, I’ll feel like I have to open the camera preview and check, then maybe change the angle or the lighting, fix my hair around that side of my face, take another picture… and then I end up doing it again. Sometimes I’ll ask a friend if I look strange, even though I know that probably puts them in an awkward position.

I try to tell myself it’ll just be one quick check, but it can keep going until I’m late or just too drained to want to go. Is that the kind of urge you mean?
Do you think your face actually looks uneven or puffy, or is it more that you're afraid it might look that way to others?

I mean… I do think it looks uneven and kind of puffy, especially the left side. I know that probably sounds more certain than I should be, because people keep telling me they don’t really see what I’m talking about.

But on video calls, or in photos from salsa, it just jumps out at me. I’ll see it and think, “That looks wrong,” like my face isn’t balanced. So I guess it’s both — I feel like I see it, and then I get really afraid other people are seeing it too and just not saying anything.

That’s actually a big part of why I came in… it’s starting to affect work and social stuff more than I’d like to admit.
Is your concern about your face limited to the left side or do you also worry about other parts of your body?

Mostly it’s the left side of my face. I don’t really have the same level of worry about other parts of my body.

It’s just… on video calls, or when I see photos from salsa, that side looks uneven or puffy to me, and then I have a hard time not focusing on it. I know people keep telling me they don’t see anything, so I feel a little silly saying it out loud, but it’s been bothering me enough that it’s starting to affect work and social things.
Is there something specific about the left side of your face that you're trying to fix or improve when you check it?

I guess I’m trying to make it look… more even? Less swollen-looking on that side, especially before I’m on a video call or if I know there might be photos, like at salsa.

It’s not one tiny spot exactly. It’s more that the left side of my face looks puffy or off-balance to me, and then I get stuck trying to fix my hair or angle my face so it doesn’t show. I know other people say they don’t see it, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but it’s hard for me to stop focusing on it. It’s been affecting work and going out more than I’d like.
Is there a specific feature or flaw on the left side of your face that you're most concerned about?

Not one feature exactly… I mean, I don’t think it’s like my nose or my eye by itself. It’s more the whole left side looking uneven or puffy to me, especially on video calls or in salsa photos.

I know everyone keeps saying they don’t see it, so I feel kind of embarrassed making such a big deal out of it. But I came in because I can’t really stop focusing on it, and it’s starting to get in the way at work and socially. Does that make sense?
Do you think others would notice the unevenness or puffiness on the left side of your face if you didn't try to hide or fix it?

I… I guess part of me thinks they would notice it if I didn’t try to hide it, especially on video calls or in salsa photos. But then everyone keeps telling me they don’t see anything, so I don’t know if I’m just over-focusing on it.

That’s kind of why I came in, because I can’t stop looking at how uneven or puffy the left side of my face seems to me. I’m sorry, I know it probably sounds minor, but it’s starting to affect work and social stuff more than I’d like.
Is your concern about the left side of your face focused on a specific flaw that you think is there, or is it more about how you feel you look overall when you see that side of your face?

It’s more about how I feel I look overall when I see that side, I think. I don’t have one specific flaw I can point to and say “that’s it.” It’s just that the left side looks uneven and kind of puffy to me, especially on video calls or in salsa photos.

I know people tell me they don’t see anything, so I feel a little silly saying it, but I came in because I can’t really stop focusing on it. And it’s starting to interfere with work and being social more than I want it to.
Do you think your perception of your face being uneven or puffy is based on how you actually look, or is it something that you feel regardless of how you might actually appear to others?

I think… I want to say it’s based on how I actually look, because when I see myself on a video call or in salsa photos it really does look uneven and puffy to me. But at the same time, everyone keeps telling me they don’t see anything, so I guess I’m not completely sure.

It feels very real to me, even if other people don’t notice it. And I’m a little embarrassed saying that, but I came in because I just can’t stop focusing on it, and it’s starting to mess with my work and social life. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think you would still be concerned about the left side of your face if you were alone and didn't have to interact with anyone?

Yeah… I think I probably would still be concerned, even if I were alone. Maybe not in the exact same way, because there wouldn’t be anyone seeing me, but I’d still notice it when I caught my face on a screen or in a photo.

It’s like I can’t stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side looks to me, even though people keep saying they don’t see it. I know that sounds a little excessive, sorry, but it’s been hard to shut off. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would still feel the need to check and fix your face if you were certain that no one would ever see you or comment on your appearance?

I think… honestly, yes, probably. I wish I could say no, because that would make more sense, but I still think I’d check.

Before meetings or going out, I keep opening the camera preview and trying different angles or lighting, and I’ll fix my hair around that side of my face. Sometimes I retake pictures a bunch of times or ask friends if I look strange. I try not to make it a big deal, but it can make me late, or by the end I’m just too drained to go.

Sorry, I know that sounds kind of… excessive. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
